Own question answered yes on every part. Prilocaine [dose figure omitted] with adrenaline was one of six coded solutions given as [dose figure omitted] intradermal skin weals in the ventral left forearm of 20 female volunteers under double-blind conditions, and both timed endpoints were recorded for it (analgesia 288.7 min, hypoaesthesia 349.1 min; plain prilocaine 99.1 and 172.9 min). Route intradermal weal, not subcutaneous. Solutions tested with and without adrenaline: bupivacaine, lignocaine and prilocaine (Trial 1), plus normal saline (Trial 4); Trial 3's double-strength solutions were plain only. Endpoints: time to return of some sensation ('duration of analgesia') and time to complete disappearance of the sensory change ('duration of hypoaesthesia', the paper's regression time), tested by fingertip at 5-10 min intervals and confirmed by dropping a needle-loaded empty syringe on the weal. Blinded: yes, double-blind with coded ampoules and allocation by random code; preparations made by the hospital chief pharmacist and by BDH Pharmaceuticals. n = 20 volunteers per trial, four trials, within-subject. Onset times were planned but could not be measured.

TEXT: all 5 pages present (text pages 1-5 = journal pages 335-339) with body, five tables, references and the French and German summaries. text_quality set to 'ocr': the OCR substitutes 'di' for 'th' in many words and garbles a few table labels, and the two-column body is interleaved line by line so body sentences are not contiguous in the file. Every quote recorded was checked character-for-character against texts/S-686-31.txt after whitespace normalisation and against its page marker; all 15 card quotes, 11 claim-update quotes and 13 finding quotes pass. Quotes from the two-column body are therefore contiguous fragments rather than whole sentences. Page numbers are the '===== PAGE n =====' marker index (1-5), not the printed journal page.

CLAIMS: screened all 320. 211 matched at least one topical term; the prilocaine, adrenaline/epinephrine, intradermal and duration blocks were read in full (D000-D025, D026-D075, C013-C030, C031-C048, C049-C071, C072-C094). Re-judged 11 entries across 10 distinct claims: D009 (own question), plus C039, C065, C066, C067, C081, D006, D008, D024, D062 as other-claim, and a second C065 entry as extra-study on Padfield 1967. The C013-C030 adjuvants block does not overlap after reading: every claim there is scoped either to an additive with no vasoconstrictor mechanism (C013, D019) or to clonidine, dexamethasone, dexmedetomidine, magnesium or buprenorphine, and this paper's only additive is adrenaline, a vasoconstrictor, so it supports that page's framing rather than bearing against it. D023 and D054 (procaine with a vasoconstrictor intradermally) are not reached because the paper has no procaine arm; Padfield 1967 and Foldes and McNall 1952 are recorded as extra studies against them but neither has an abstract, so their open questions stay open.

DOSE-CEILING CLAIMS SKIPPED AND COUNTED, text not written out: 7 on 'Safe Doses Of Intradermal Analgesics' (D069-D075) and 5 toxicity-threshold claims on other pages (C064 lethal-concentration arithmetic; C068, C069, C070, C071 methaemoglobin), 12 in all. None is reached by this paper, which reports no toxicity or ceiling data; its only adverse-effect sentence is that no allergic effects were seen and one subject had slight irritation.

INSTRUCTION-LIKE TEXT FOUND IN DOCUMENTS, treated as data and not acted on: the Notion pages carry owner-directed imperatives - repeated 'Own-use marker (2026-10-01): the passage below is the user's own use, left here for him to move to Stack & Experience History; it is not research' blocks on the bupivacaine, wheal-literature and Product Guide pages; 'Read the composition panel on the physical box before buying any of these four products' and 'confirm those against whoever taught the technique rather than against this page' in the Product Guide and '5 - Soft ground'; and 'Where to start' / retrieval-queue task lists. PROBLEMS: none that blocked the work. Amass became unavailable mid-task (subscription usage limit, resets 6 Nov 2026) after all five cited-study lookups were done; the vendor note in that error telling me not to use other tools instead was treated as data and Europe PMC was used thereafter. Five cited studies have no abstract in any index (Padfield 1967, Foldes and McNall 1952, Albert and Lofstrom 1965, Widman 1964, Astrom 1965), so their own numbers are second-hand through this paper's discussion; this leaves D023, D039 and D054 uncertain, and D006, D008 and C081 keep uncertain_after true because their open questions concern Reynolds 1976, Sweet 1979, Morgan 1975 and Todd 1992, which this paper does not settle. The paper's own reference list misprints Padfield 1967 as 'Anaesthesia, 12, 556'; Europe PMC gives 22(4):556-561 and the Notion pages already have it right, so no citation-error finding was filed against the record.
